messages:
elaine: Quick sync — I'm kicking off a 10% random sampling of principals that have admin/owner roles to validate delegated permissions and KMS key entitlements. Sharing the SQL-ish query I'm using for the IAM export: ```SELECT principal, role, resource, last_active FROM iam_bindings WHERE role ILIKE '%admin%' OR role ILIKE '%owner%' ORDER BY random() LIMIT 1000;```

samir: solid. can we also flag service accounts vs human users and tag any principal with 'last_active > 180 days' for follow-up? add a column for key_access_count too if possible. :mag:

elaine: yes — adding filters now. will mark service accounts with `sa:true`. goal is to hand ~10% sample to app owners for attestation, and separately run a focused KMS entitlement check for any principal that shows up with key_access_count > 0.

marta: for the KMS check, can we get a quick mapping of which keys are customer-controlled vs platform? last time we found a couple of keys that were used by dashboards and had overly broad roles.

elaine: mapped. I'm pulling `kms_key_id, owner_team, usage_count, acl` from the key inventory. plan: if owner_team = platform -> require rotation plan + narrower IAM binding. if owner_team != platform -> ping owners for justification.

audit-bot: automated note — exported 1,024 iam_bindings rows to /tmp/iam_export_1728991234.csv (sha256: b94d27b9934). No privileged principal with `last_active IS NULL` in sample.

samir: good call. for the attestation email, please include a one-click response: Approve / Revoke / Needs more info. we'll treat no-response after 7 days as 'needs more info' and escalate to manager.

elaine: adding that to the attestation template. also adding a short repro for audit logs we can attach: example event where a dashboard svcacct requested decrypt on customer-key: ```{timestamp: 2024-06-12T03:21:09Z, principal: svc-dashboard@redwood, action: kms.decrypt, key_id: projects/redwood/keys/cust-45, result: ALLOWED}```

marta: that event is helpful — can we correlate with deploy history? if that svcacct got new permissions during last sprint rollout we need to capture the change window for post-mortem.

elaine: correlating now with deploy metadata — looks like perms granted in rollout 2024-05-28 (deploy id: d-4421). I've flagged that for vuln-triage if owner doesn't justify.

devops-oncall: FYI, if we revoke any platform-level roles we should run the smoke tests for infra pipelines. last time a prune broke a prometheus exporter. recommend canary revoke on one team first.

samir: agree on canary. propose this plan: 1) run 10% sampling attestation, 2) run KMS entitlement check for those with key_access_count > 0, 3) hold canary revokes for platform roles with devops-oncall watching, 4) escalate any unjustified admin grants to security-ops for remediation.

elaine: plan noted. I'll split the sample: 75% human owner attestation, 25% service account deep-review. timeline: attestation email goes out EOD, 7 day SLA for replies, canary revokes next week. I'll post the CSV + attestation template in #eng-security docs after send.

marta: thanks — please include a short snippet in the attestation that owners should confirm whether svcacct is allowed to call kms.decrypt/kms.encrypt and to list alternatives.

elaine: will do. tagging @samir to review the revocation runbook once I post it so we can ensure rollback steps are explicit. :thumbsup:

samir: will review. also let's add an audit rule: alert on any `kms.decrypt` by a principal that is not in the key owner group for that key — set severity=medium and create ticket for >3 violations in 24h.

audit-bot: rule created: kms_decrypt_cross_owner — severity: medium, threshold: 3/24h, notify channel: #eng-security, create ticket in SECURITY queue.

elaine: perfect. I'll update the runbook and attach the sample CSV to the thread once ready. thanks all.
